PullRequest.Title: build: report a stopped 1ES Network Isolation listener on Windows
PullRequest.Body:

Related to [microsoft/vscode-engineering#4433](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/issues/4433) and [microsoft/vscode-engineering#3684](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/issues/3684).

## What changes

On Windows, 1ES Network Isolation runs `EtwNetworkEventListener.exe`, which serves both the job's HTTP proxy and its DNS. When that process exits during a job, every later download fails in a way that looks like an outage of whatever the failing step was contacting. Today a failed job then shows, for example:

```text
Checkout microsoft/vscode-capi
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-capi/': Failed to connect to github.com:443 over proxy <address> after 2056 ms: Could not connect to server
```

and the only hint of the real cause is `No service process found to kill` in the 1ES Stop Network Isolation log. After this change, the same job also reports:

```text
Collect Windows network failure diagnostics
##[error]The 1ES Network Isolation listener (EtwNetworkEventListener.exe), which serves the HTTP proxy and DNS of this job, is no longer running. Network failures after it stopped, such as "Failed to connect to github.com port 443 ... over proxy" or "No such host is known", are a Network Isolation infrastructure failure rather than a VS Code or service outage. ...
```

and its logs artifact contains bounded JSON evidence for the Network Isolation owners, including:

```json
{ "verdict": "listenerStopped", "isolationStarted": true, "listenerRunning": false,
  "proxy": { "port": 18080, "reachable": false, "connectResult": "ConnectionRefused", "connectMs": 2097 } }
```

Jobs with a healthy listener report `listenerRunning` and no error. Successful jobs don't collect anything.

## How

- `collect-network-diagnostics.ps1` collects, after a failure:
  - `listener-health`: whether Network Isolation started, whether the listener is running, and a TCP probe of the proxy port. The proxy address isn't recorded.
  - `listener-clr-exceptions`: the exception type and method-only stack frames of `.NET Runtime` crash records for the listener. Exception messages aren't kept, because they can contain proxied URLs.
  - The DNS resolver and listener evidence for DNS failures (#3684), the listener's native crash records, and an inventory of the Network Isolation log folder (names and sizes only, no contents).
- The collector is the last step of every failed Windows compile, CI, flaky-build and product test job (a shared `product-build-win32-network-diagnostics.yml` step template), so it sees failures in any step and runs before 1ES stops Network Isolation. CI, test and flaky jobs include the output in their existing logs artifact; product compile jobs publish a separate `network-diagnostics-windows-<arch>-compile-<attempt>` artifact.
- The DNS Client operational channel is disabled on the hosted images, so that expected state is recorded without a warning.
- `network-diagnostics.md` documents the evidence and how to validate changes.

This makes the failure attributable and gives the Network Isolation owners evidence; it doesn't prevent the listener from exiting or recover the job.

## Validation

Hosted validation on two temporary, non-publishing Windows CI runs of this branch, each with one step injected before `Checkout microsoft/vscode-capi` (the injected steps are not part of this PR):

- **Listener stopped:** the injected step stopped `EtwNetworkEventListener.exe`. In all seven Windows jobs, the real vscode-capi checkout then failed with the same message and ~2 s connect time as the production failures, the collector reported `listenerStopped` with the error above, and Stop Network Isolation logged `No service process found to kill`. Isolation stayed enforced (the firewall filters remained); only the job's own traffic failed.
- **Control:** the injected step just failed. The collector reported `listenerRunning` with a reachable proxy and no listener error.
- On the hosted agents, every section was collected except the always-disabled DNS Client operational channel. The crash-record sections were empty in both runs, as expected for a stopped (not crashed) process, so they're validated only by unit tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Successful Windows compile, CI, flaky-build, and product-test jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Azure evaluates the added template step's `failed()` condition, but the collector subprocess and compile diagnostic artifact output do not run; successful job completion has no new diagnostic work on its critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One condition evaluation per Windows job; the number of product-test jobs can be several, but each successful job skips the body independently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No collector process is launched. Existing Windows jobs retain their prior cross-job parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is consulted or populated by the added diagnostics; cold and warm dependency-cache behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added step and compile artifact both have explicit failure conditions, and tests assert failure-only placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Only negligible pipeline-template/condition evaluation remains; no changed expensive boundary is reachable.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: successful build and test critical paths do not execute the new subprocess, probes, event queries, serialization, or artifact upload.

Scenarios.Scenario: Failed Windows compile, combined CI, or flaky-build job
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After all prior user steps fail, one diagnostic step runs before Network Isolation teardown and delays failed-job completion until it finishes or the 45-second process-tree deadline expires. Any configured failure artifact publication follows it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Node launches one PowerShell collector under the existing process-tree timeout helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One Node-to-PowerShell launch per failed job attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Failed jobs proceeded directly to existing output publication and Network Isolation teardown without this collector.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on the failed-job completion path and is bounded to 45 seconds, with a two-minute task backstop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: A TCP connection probes the configured HTTP/HTTPS proxy endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one probe per invocation when a valid HTTP proxy URI exists; wait is capped at five seconds and observed refusal is normally about two seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds bounded latency only after the job has already failed and supplies the listener-health verdict.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: PowerShell queries process, DNS server, UDP endpoint, TCP connection, and Windows event-log state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two process enumerations, one DNS-server query, one UDP-endpoint query, one TCP-connection query, and up to four log metadata plus four bounded event queries per failed job; event results stop at 65 and the hosted disabled DNS Operational channel skips its event query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These OS-state and event-log queries were not performed by the jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Sequentially contributes to the collector's bounded failure-path latency; none is on successful-job progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates the diagnostics directory, writes initial placeholders and final JSON sections, and inventories immediate listener-log metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Eleven bounded JSON files, approximately 22 writes including placeholder replacement/final capture, plus one immediate-directory enumeration stopped after 65 files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No network-diagnostic JSON files or listener-log metadata inventory were created.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small bounded local I/O on failed-job completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serializes each diagnostic record to JSON before enforcing the 64 KiB persisted-file limit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded serialization per write; record collections are capped at 64 and nested DNS addresses at 64 per capped interface.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded CPU/allocation on the failure path; inputs cannot grow with job history beyond the explicit record limits.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Publishes the compile diagnostic directory as a pipeline artifact; CI and flaky jobs add these files to their pre-existing logs artifact.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one new compile artifact per failed attempt, with at most eleven files of 64 KiB each; CI/flaky publication call count is unchanged and only gains bounded bytes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Compile jobs had no network-diagnostic artifact; CI/flaky jobs already uploaded `.build/logs` but without these files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds a small bounded upload after failed compile jobs; existing CI/flaky log publication was already on their completion path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one collector invocation per failed job attempt. Each invocation caps section records at 64, output files at 64 KiB, and total runtime at 45 seconds; aggregate work scales with the number of concurrently failed jobs, which run on separate agents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The PowerShell collector performs its sections sequentially. There is one collector per job; parallel CI/flaky jobs can each run one on their own agents, with no within-agent burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no cache. Every failed attempt captures a fresh snapshot and first overwrites sections with `notCollected`; no cold/warm distinction or retry amplification occurs inside one attempt.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: template reachability, sequential call flow, source-side event caps, output caps, and timeout semantics were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact Windows cmdlet and event-log latency varies by hosted image state, but the one-per-failed-attempt cardinality and 45-second hard deadline are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added latency and bounded I/O are intentional diagnostic work restricted to already-failed jobs, with one invocation per attempt, no fan-out by event/item, and hard runtime/output bounds.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The final failure-only diagnostic step runs after setup/download/test steps and before teardown; its completion is required before the job's existing always-published logs artifact can finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runs the same bounded Node/PowerShell collector as the final product-test step.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One launch for each failed standalone product-test attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test job moved directly from its test steps to existing outputs/teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds up to 45 seconds after failure before existing log artifact publication and teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing `.build/logs` pipeline artifact upload now includes the bounded network diagnostic files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Upload call count remains one per job; payload increases by no more than roughly 704 KiB from eleven 64 KiB files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same logs artifact was uploaded without the new network snapshot.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only bounded additional upload bytes; artifact publication already occurred unconditionally.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invocation per failed product-test job attempt. A product build may have several test jobs, but each invocation is independently bounded and concurrent jobs execute on separate agents.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Sections are sequential within a job. Multiple failed product-test jobs may collect concurrently only through the pipeline's existing job-level parallelism.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or coalescing exists or is needed across isolated job agents; each failed attempt records current state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the template is the last job step and the existing logs output condition and path were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneously failing test jobs varies by build configuration, but per-job work and output are hard-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: deliberate post-failure diagnostics add bounded per-job latency and bytes without changing successful test execution or introducing per-test-case fan-out.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The added Node test file runs isolated PowerShell collector fixtures synchronously; the interruption fixture invokes the timeout helper and intentionally waits for its deadline before assertions continue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawns isolated PowerShell collectors, with one case nesting the Node timeout helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One synchronous child per test fixture, twelve in the current suite; one timeout fixture is deliberately held for five seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test file and its child-process work did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds seconds to the focused Windows-only test command, but does not execute in product jobs or non-Windows test runs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Creates fixture trees/files, reads bounded JSON outputs, and removes each temporary tree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small isolated tree per fixture, plus 70 files in the explicit limit fixture.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bounded local test-only I/O serialized with each fixture.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Twelve collector fixtures are run serially on Windows, including one five-second timeout case; the suite is skipped on non-Windows platforms.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `spawnSync` serializes all fixture processes. The local loopback server tests do not create an unbounded concurrent workload.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each fixture uses a fresh temporary directory and process, so there is no warm cache; this isolation is deliberate test behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: synchronous spawn calls and the explicit five-second deadline are direct in the added test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: PowerShell startup time varies by Windows runner; the timeout fixture contributes a known five-second floor.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the cost is confined to the new focused Windows-only validation, is fixed and bounded, and the longer deadline supports reliable observation of partially written interruption state rather than affecting product or general successful pipeline execution.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and transitive pipeline/timeout paths. The change adds bounded, sequential diagnostics only after Windows job failures; successful paths skip them. OS queries, one proxy probe, JSON/file work, and artifact bytes were counted and compared with prior behavior. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found, and the PR does not fix a prior shipped performance regression.
